what: Which decoder layers carry the int8 error: fp32 torch on MPS (S = 64 chunks, the oracle's ids and image rows, the author's head), the exporter's own int8 weights swapped in per config, on the six runs where int8lin breaks the bar worst. The rule was written (bisect/rule.json) before any bisect result; configs with outside_rule_search = true were run after the fixed search and never selected by it.

removed: configs.*.runs.*.questions[].probs (each question keeps max |dp| and the argmax flag)
trimmed.full_copies: the source files above, in the lane directory $ZOO_WORK_ROOT/_clefflash/ (not in the repository)

rule.1: worst bisect run max|dp| <= 0.010 (every option of every question, near-ties included)
rule.2: no bisect run's max|dp| above its own int8lin value (this instrument)
rule.4: the smallest layer set meeting 1-3; between sets of one size, the lexicographically smallest sorted layer list
rule.search: int8lin, exact, fp16 L00-15, fp16 L16-31, only GDN int8, only attention int8, only MLP int8, one layer fp16 at a time (32); then candidate sets: layers ranked by their single-layer worst-run max|dp| (ties: the lower index); for k = 2..6 the top-k set; at the first k whose top-k set meets 1-3, also every other k-subset of the top k+1; stop there. A single layer meeting 1-3 ends the search at size 1 (every single is evaluated).

rule.why_runs: launch rule 'the runs that break the bar + the worst 3, <= 6': int8lin pf64 (results/readout_int8lin_pf64.json) breaks max|dp| 0.02 on 9 runs; these are the 6 worst of them (0.0748, 0.0295, 0.0265, 0.0255, 0.0238, 0.0235)

bisect.instrument: fp32 torch (parity_decoder_torch.Runner), S = 64 chunks from fresh zero states, oracle ids + oracle fp32 image_embeds, the author's fp32 head; per config the listed modules carry the exporter's int8 weights (quantize_pytorch_model on the fp16 model, dequantized by the finalized module), every other quantizable module its exact checkpoint weight
